newsitem.title: USA: San Diego set to issue stadium bonds - official.
newsitem.headline: San Diego set to issue stadium bonds - official.

text.p: A California state Supreme Court decision has cleared the way for San Diego to issue about $67 million of revenue bonds to expand its football and baseball stadium, city officials said Friday.
The city plans to come to market in the first week of December with $66.6 million of lease revenue bonds, which would be taxable, City Manager Jack McGrory said.
The city council already approved the bond issue, which was not put to a vote of the public, McGrory said.

Due to litigation-related delays and rising labor and construction material costs, the city expects to re-enter the market with a second bond to raise additional funds, McGrory said. The second issue would be for $10 million or more.

The State Supreme Court, in a decision hailed by city officials, declined a request by tax activists to review a lower court decision on the project. The deal's opponents had sought to have the proposed stadium bond issue placed before San Diego voters.
"That's the end of the litigation," McGrory said of the state Supreme Court decision.
The stadium expansion is expected to begin by mid-January, after the football season ends. The project should be completed by Sept 1, 1997. The project would add about 10,000 seats to the stadium.
Under the plan, McGrory said the bonds would be repaid with revenues generated at Jack Murphy Stadium from professional football and baseball games.
